title: Architecture Stewardship Recertification
stop_condition: MULTIPLE — S213 (Broken traceability, Duplicate registry creation), S214 (Registry authority conflict, Duplicate registry creation), S215 (Governance Guard != PASS, Principle violation, Broken traceability)

inputs.s213: SESSION213_DRIFT_SIMULATION_RESULTS.json — 6/6 drift categories present, 4/6 scenarios detected, mean response quality 1.67/5, overall CONCERN
inputs.s214: SESSION214_REGISTRY_STRESS_TEST.json — 1/6 registries with single source, 5/6 with duplicate ownership, overall CONCERN
inputs.s215: SESSION215_TECHNICAL_DEBT_STATUS.json — 2/8 TD items resolved, 5 open, highest learner-safety risk HIGH (DL-016), Stop Condition Compliance FAIL

drift_prevention.rationale: 66.7% detection rate with mean response quality of 1.67/5. 2 of 6 categories undetectable by current controls. 3 of 6 categories have zero automated enforcement.

registry_integrity.rationale: Only 1 of 6 registries has confirmed single-source-of-truth. 5 registries have 2-8 competing authoritative sources each. Active conflicts include 40-item pipeline divergence (DL-036) and 267-item certification count gap.

debt_reduction.rationale: 2 of 8 TD items resolved. Core structural enforcement (DL-008, DL-026) is strong with 0 Certified exposure. But 5 open items include HIGH learner-safety risk (DL-016: 58 Certified items), missing infrastructure (safe_rebuild.js), and stale reference data.

stop_condition_compliance.rationale: 1 of 6 stop conditions fully met, 1 partially met, 4 fully unmet. Framework cannot detect registry authority conflicts, broken traceability, duplicate registry creation, or identity violations.

scalability.rationale: Per-write guard parsing scales. 30-item batch cap adds overhead. SOURCE_FILE_RE hardcoded to Part 1 naming — Part 2 files would bypass all rules. No Part 2 planning documented.

sustainability.rationale: Single point of failure (governance guard). No backup enforcement automation. REVISION_HISTORY at 23,364 lines with no TOC. Missing safe_rebuild.js. WARN-level rules allow silent compliance gaps.

operational_resilience.rationale: DL-019 concurrent-write vulnerability unresolved. Bash bypasses governance guard. Admin platform files (11 new) lack baseline entries. Stale reference documents propagated as current.

determination_rationale: The S208 Framework v2 architecture is structurally sound in its core enforcement (DL-008, DL-026 blocked at the write gate, 32/32 test suite). However, the framework fails to meet 5 of 6 automatic stop conditions and cannot detect or prevent the drift patterns that are actively occurring in the live workspace. Stewardship recertification cannot proceed until the 4 unmet stop conditions are addressed (identity, traceability, registry conflicts, duplicate registries), the stale reference data is corrected (SESSION_STATUS, CURRENT_BASELINES, AGENTS.md §9), and the missing infrastructure is created (safe_rebuild.js, file-lock protocol, backup enforcement).
required_remediation: 1. Upgrade Rules 1 and 4 from WARN to BLOCK level
2. Add identity validator rule (minimum: CorrectChoice, Stem, ExplanationCorrect, Choices fields present)
3. Add cross-registry reconciliation at session startup
4. Create missing scripts/safe_rebuild.js or remove stale reference
5. Update CURRENT_BASELINES.md §4 to document Rule 6 and 32-test count
6. Update AGENTS.md §9 to deprecate SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24.md reference
8. Extend SOURCE_FILE_RE to accept Part 2 naming conventions
9. Add admin platform files to CURRENT_BASELINES.md (11 files)
12. Remediate DL-016 (58 Certified items with metadata-block shift)
13. Remediate DL-035 (39 Certified Domain F items with empty EW slots)
